bihar_raw_news.title: Supreme Court Upholds Promotees' Seniority in Bihar Police Service - Lawtext
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Judgement Scroll Down To Discover Supreme Court Supreme Court Upholds Promotees' Seniority in Bihar Police Service — Validity of Gradation List Affirmed. In Favour of Accused Admin 2026-10-10 16:34:11 6 Share This Article: Font size: Print Case Note & Summary The dispute arose from the promotion and seniority of police officers in the Bihar Police Service. The appellants, who were appointed as Inspectors of Police in 1953, were promoted to officiate as Deputy Superintendents of Police in 1965. After a prolonged period of officiation, the State Government confirmed their promotions in 1974, but later issued a gradation list placing them below direct recruits appointed in 1974. The appellants challenged this list in the Patna High Court, which directed the State Government to re-examine the matter based on recommendations from the Saran Singh Committee. The State Government subsequently issued a revised gradation list, which the appellants contested. The Supreme Court examined the legality of the gradation list and the basis for determining seniority between promotees and direct recruits. The court found that the State Government had the authority to regulate public services under its executive power in the absence of specific legislation. It upheld the principle of continuous officiation as a valid basis for seniority, rejecting claims that the gradation list violated Article 14 of the Constitution. The court also clarified that Rule 3 of the Bihar Police Service (Recruitment) Rules did not impose a fixed quota for promotions and that filling more than half of the vacancies with promotees was permissible. Ultimately, the Supreme Court allowed the appeals, set aside the High Court's judgment, and dismissed the writ petitions, ordering corrections to the gradation list where necessary. Headnote A) Constitutional Law - Regulation of Public Services - State Government's Executive Power - The State Government can regulate its public services in the absence of legislation or rules under Article 309. The court held that the State's actions in determining seniority based on continuous officiation were valid as no statutory rule existed to the contrary. (Paras 456 F-G, 457 A) B) Seniority - Continuous Officiation as Basis - The determination of seniority based on continuous officiation has been upheld as valid. The court found that the gradation list could not be challenged on grounds of arbitrary dates or violation of Article 14. (Paras 456 G-H, 457 A) C) Recruitment Rules - Interpretation of Rule 3 - Rule 3 of the Bihar Police Service (Recruitment) Rules does not prescribe a fixed quota but ensures that at least half of the vacancies are filled by promotees. The court ruled that filling more than half of the vacancies by promotees does not violate this rule. (Paras 457 G-H, 458 A-B) D) Correction of Gradation List - The court noted that the gradation list contained mistakes that should be corrected by the concerned authority. bihar_raw_news.content: Policy 1 min read ICC sets sights on accelerating Bihar’s industrial growth and investment climate ICC appoints a new Chairman for its Bihar State Council, aiming to boost industrial growth, attract investments, strengthen MSMEs and startups, and deepen industry-government collaboration. Online Bureau ETGovernment Published On Oct 10, 2026 at 10:21 AM IST Select ETGovernment as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Prabhat Kumar Sinha The Indian Chamber of Commerce (ICC) has appointed Prabhat Kumar Sinha as Chairman of its Bihar State Council, reinforcing the Chamber’s commitment to promoting industrial development, attracting investments and strengthening industry-government collaboration in the state. The appointment was announced by Parthiv Neotia, President of the Indian Chamber of Commerce, during the Chamber’s Annual General Meeting (AGM) held in Kolkata. Congratulating Sinha on his new responsibility, Neotia expressed confidence that his leadership would contribute to strengthening Bihar’s industrial ecosystem, improving the investment climate and expanding engagement between industry stakeholders and the state government. Advt Sinha brings experience in industrial development, investment promotion, information technology, MSMEs, entrepreneurship and policy-related initiatives. He has been actively associated with industry and government stakeholders in Bihar, particularly in areas concerning ease of doing business, technology adoption and the development of a more competitive business environment. Speaking on his appointment, Sinha emphasised the opportunities emerging from Bihar’s ongoing economic transformation and outlined his priorities for the ICC Bihar State Council. He said the Council would focus on facilitating investments, supporting entrepreneurs and startups, strengthening industry-government coordination and creating employment opportunities. The appointment comes at a time when Bihar is seeking to accelerate industrialisation, diversify its economic base and attract greater private investment. Improving infrastructure, expanding manufacturing capabilities, encouraging technology-driven enterprises and strengthening the MSME sector will be important elements in sustaining the state's economic growth. Under Sinha’s leadership, the ICC Bihar State Council is expected to play a more active role in facilitating dialogue between policymakers and industry representatives, identifying investment opportunities and addressing challenges faced by businesses. The Council will also seek to encourage entrepreneurship and promote an investment-friendly environment capable of supporting industrial expansion and employment generation. national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 147 India slams Pakistan at UN, reiterates J&K is an integral and inalienable part of the country
national_raw_news.content: India slammed Pakistan at the United Nations for spreading lies and falsehoods about Jammu and Kashmir, asserting that the Union Territory is, and will always remain, an integral and inalienable part of India. India exercised its Right of Reply during a discussion on decolonisation in the Fourth Committee of the UN General Assembly in New York today. Member of Parliament Mahima Kumari Mewar responded to a statement by Pakistan’s representative. In a post on X, India at the UN in New York said Mewar had accused Pakistan of misusing the UN platform to spread false claims about Jammu and Kashmir. Mewar also highlighted human rights violations by Pakistan in areas under its illegal occupation and asked Islamabad to address the situation. She said that Pakistani forces and their proxies had killed civilians protesting for their rights and basic necessities. Meanwhile, Member of Parliament Priya Saroj delivered India’s national statement at the 81st session of the UN General Assembly’s Sixth Committee on Agenda Item 75, concerning the criminal accountability of United Nations officials and experts on mission. According to India at the UN, Saroj underscored India’s zero-tolerance approach towards criminal conduct and misconduct by personnel. She also called for stronger cooperation between the United Nations and member states, along with effective accountability mechanisms. India has also warned Pakistan that it will not be deterred by nuclear threats and will deliver a fitting response to any terrorist attack. India’s senior adviser to the Permanent Mission to the UN Conference on Disarmament in Geneva, Anmol Sher Bedi, made the remarks while speaking at the United Nations General Assembly’s First Committee meeting in New York yesterday. He said India would make no distinction between those who sponsor terrorism and those who mastermind it. Referring to Operation Sindoor, launched last year following the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 civilians in Jammu and Kashmir, Mr Bedi said India had acted in self-defence through measured and targeted actions designed to avoid escalation. He stressed that nuclear weapons must not be used as instruments of routine state policy and warned that using nuclear threats to shield terrorist activities could increase the risk of escalation. Mr Bedi also raised concerns over nuclear proliferation, citing the history of the Abdul Qadeer Khan network, and urged countries to exercise caution while engaging in nuclear and advanced military cooperation with Pakistan.

national_raw_news.title: AQM reviews stubble burning prevention measures with district administrations of Amritsar ...
national_raw_news.content: CAQM reviews stubble burning prevention measures with district administrations of Amritsar and Tarn Taran Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर CAQM reviews stubble burning prevention measures with district administrations of Amritsar and Tarn Taran ANI | Updated: Oct 10, 2026 21:31 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 10 (ANI): A high-level team of the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas ( CAQM ), under the chairmanship of Dr. S D Attri, Member (Technical), CAQM , visited Amritsar and Tarn Taran Districts of Punjab during the ongoing paddy harvesting season. According to the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, these districts have been identified as hotspots for paddy stubble burning. Apart from field visits, the visiting team held a review meeting in Amritsar today with Deputy Commissioners (DCs) and other district-level officials of Amritsar and Tarn Taran districts. This visit, apart from the deployment of flying squads, is in line with the high priority attached by the commission towards achieving the objective of reduction and elimination of paddy stubble burning, a major cause of winter air pollution in NCR and adjoining areas. The deliberations focused on reviewing preparedness and coordination among the concerned departments and district administration for effective in-situ and ex-situ utilisation of paddy stubble. The commission stressed the importance of facilitating the farmers in terms of timely availability of CRM Machines, sensitising, conducting Information, Education and Communication (IEC) Activities and providing necessary support. Along with the review meeting, CAQM undertook field visits on October 9 and October 10 to the selected hotspot villages and facilities in the districts of Amritsar and Tarn Taran to assess the prevailing ground-level situation and review the implementation of measures aimed at preventing stubble burning. Regarding the district of Amritsar , the deliberations during the review meeting and field visit included the harvesting and procurement status, along with the availability and deployment of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery, said the ministry. It was informed that balers from Amritsar and adjoining districts were operating for collection and management of paddy straw. A supply chain has been established with industries having boilers for utilisation of paddy straw bales, with farmers and aggregators linked to these industries to facilitate ex-situ management. The district has also established a Control Room and Help Desk at the District Administrative Complex to identify farmers requiring CRM machinery and facilitate its availability. A district-level helpline has been circulated for reporting fire and stubble burning incidents to enable prompt action. Regarding the district of Tarn Taran, the deliberations during the review meeting and field visit included the harvesting and procurement status and the availability and deployment of CRM machinery in the district. It was informed that balers from Tarn Taran and adjoining districts were operating for effective ex-situ management of paddy straw and that the district had substantially achieved its targets regarding procurement and availability of CRM machinery for farmers. To use standard view, enable JavaScript by changing your browser options. होम सभी विशेषताएं विशेषताएं विवरण Infrastructure From Beacons to Landmarks: India’s Changing Lighthouse Story Posted On: 10 OCT 2026 3:17PM For generations, India's lighthouses were places people saw from a distance. Standing at the edge of the sea, they marked dangerous stretches of coast and guided vessels through darkness. Their lights belonged to sailors. Their towers belonged to the landscape. With a coastline stretching over 11,000 km and 205 lighthouses , India is now reimagining these historic maritime guardians. Today, the lighthouse is becoming much more than a distant landmark. Its first purpose remains unchanged: helping vessels navigate safely along India's coastline. Around that enduring role, however, a new chapter is taking shape. Lighthouse stations are being upgraded and opened to the public. Their maritime stories are finding space in museums, while their surroundings are being developed with pathways, gardens, amphitheatres and other facilities. Modern systems are strengthening the infrastructure that keeps their lights working reliably. Lighthouse tourism has risen from about 4 lakh visitors in 2014 to 18.63 lakh in 2024–25 . Across the country, 75 lighthouses have been developed as tourism destinations to preserve their historical and architectural significance. Some of these include the Mandvi Lighthouse and Dwarka Lighthouse in Gujarat, Tadri Lighthouse in Karnataka, Pamban Lighthouse in Tamil Nadu, and Vizhinjam Lighthouse in Kerala. A digital ticketing portal has also been launched under the Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships (DGLL), bringing the visitor experience onto a common digital platform. The growing interest in lighthouse tourism is creating new spaces to showcase India’s maritime legacy. These developments have also generated employment with nearby hotels, restaurants, tour operators, transport services, local shops, and artisans. The Light Still Leads The lighthouse may look much the same from a distance, but the technology behind its familiar beam has changed significantly. What once depended on fire and oil is now powered by the sun and strengthened by modern technology. All lighthouses in the country are solar-powered, making renewable energy part of the infrastructure that keeps these navigational lights working. The evolution can be traced through individual stations. At Samiyani Island in Gujarat, an oil lamp gave way to a solar-powered electronic flasher, followed by an LED lantern in 2016. At Jodiya, a solar-operated flashing light was introduced before being upgraded to a high-intensity LED lantern in 2021. Lighthouses have become part of India's wider maritime information network. 87 Automatic Identification System (AIS) shore stations have been installed on lighthouses along the coast. This ensures that the beam remains dependable, responsive and ready to guide vessels safely. AIS is a ship and shore-based data broadcast system in accordance with SOLAS (International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea).
